claims.text: The starting material is an approximately 1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy-alloy multilayer coating produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
A modulation period of 16 nm produces semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces containing misfit dislocations.
The 8 nm multilayer has fully coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes.
The 32 and 80 nm multilayers have grain-boundary-dominated structures.
Semicoherent interfaces strongly impede dislocation glide.
Blocked dislocation glide causes local dislocation pileups and stress concentrations.
Localized stresses at the semicoherent interfaces can induce interfacial amorphization during sustained loading.
Interfacial amorphization creates free volume, structural disorder, and high-energy crystal-amorphous boundaries.
The amorphized interfacial structure lowers atomic-migration barriers.
Lower migration barriers cause creep to shift from dislocation slip or climb toward atomic-diffusion- or interface-slip-controlled deformation.
The mechanism transition associated with the 16 nm period improves room-temperature creep resistance.
The 16 nm multilayer will have the highest room-temperature creep resistance among the 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm samples.
The 16 nm multilayer will exhibit a creep stress exponent near 1–2.
A creep stress exponent near 1–2 indicates diffusion- or interface-slip-controlled creep.
The 8, 32, and 80 nm multilayers will exhibit creep stress exponents greater than 3.
A creep stress exponent greater than 3 indicates predominantly dislocation-mediated creep.
The 8, 32, and 80 nm baseline multilayers exhibit predominantly dislocation-mediated creep.
The proposed comparison varies modulation period among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm while using room-temperature nanoindentation creep at a maximum load of 5 mN.
The intended testing window uses a 100 s load hold and indentation depths of approximately one-tenth to one-seventh of the coating thickness.
Direct observation of stress-induced interfacial amorphization under sustained loading remains unverified and would require additional microscopy.
